Adaptation
An inherited feature that helps an organism survive and reproduce in its usual environment.
Amphibian
An animal belonging to the group that includes frogs and toads; many use water and land during their lives.
Aquatic
Living in water, or describing a habitat in water.
Biodiversity
The variety of living things found in a region.
Climber
A plant that grows upwards using external support.
Cotyledon
A seed leaf that is part of the embryo inside a seed.
Creeper
A plant with stems that trail along the ground.
Dicot
A flowering plant whose seed has two cotyledons.
Endosperm
Food-storing tissue in a seed that nourishes the developing embryo.
Fibrous root system
A spreading bunch of roots without one dominant main root.
Grouping
Arranging things by features they share, using a stated rule.
Habitat
The place where an organism lives, including its conditions and resources.
Herb
A plant with soft, non-woody stems; it need not be small.
Monocot
A flowering plant whose seed has one cotyledon.
Parallel venation
A leaf-vein pattern in which many veins run alongside one another.
Pseudostem
A trunk-like structure formed by overlapping leaf bases, as in banana.
Reticulate venation
A leaf-vein pattern in which veins branch and join to form a network.
Sacred grove
A patch of vegetation protected through local cultural or religious traditions.
Shrub
A woody plant that usually branches near the ground, often with several main stems.
Taproot
The main root of a root system, with smaller roots branching from it.
Terrestrial
Living on land, or describing a habitat on land.
Tree
A woody plant that usually develops a main trunk supporting a crown of branches.
Venation
The pattern of veins in a leaf.
